title: Building Strings
goal: Learn how to format dynamic text and pre-allocate string buffers.

sections.text: You can build owned strings dynamically with the `format!` macro. It works like `println!`, but returns a new `String` instead of printing.

sections.caption: format! creates a new owned String.

sections.text: When building a string piece by piece, calling `String::new()` reallocates memory as it grows. If you know the capacity needed, use `String::with_capacity`.

sections.caption: Allocates space for 10 bytes up front.

sections.text: Raw string literals let you write quotes and backslashes without escaping. Write `r#"..."#` to include raw text directly.

sections.code:
let path = r"C:\Program Files";
let json = r#"{"key": "val"}"#;
sections.caption: Raw strings ignore escape sequences.

explanation: Learn how to format dynamic text and pre-allocate string buffers.
